stages.name: Promoting competition
stages.title: Promoting competition
stages.sub: Why governments try to open up markets to new firms, and the trade-off in helping small businesses do it.

steps.q: A huge, established supermarket chain dominates a town. A new small grocer wants to open nearby but faces enormous costs just to get started. If it were instead very cheap and easy for any new grocer to open up and start trading, would the big chain still be able to charge high prices unchallenged?
steps.right: No, it would have to compete harder
steps.wrong: Yes, size alone protects it either way
steps.hint: Think about what stops new firms entering, and what happens to the incumbent if that barrier disappears.

steps.q: A dominant firm with a lot of market power can restrict output and push up prices with little fear of new rivals entering. If a government makes that market more contestable, what is likely to happen to prices and choice for consumers?
steps.wrong: Prices and choice stay about the same
steps.hint: If new firms can now enter easily, what pressure does that put on the dominant firm's pricing?

steps.q: A government wants more small firms to be able to enter a market dominated by giants. The small firms struggle with high start-up costs, tax bills and red tape that the giants can easily absorb. What could the government do to help them enter?
steps.right: Give them grants, tax breaks or lighter regulation
steps.wrong: Raise taxes on all firms equally
steps.hint: Which of these actions specifically lowers the burden on small firms rather than everyone?

steps.q: After several small firms take up these grants and tax breaks and enter the market, is the industry now easier or harder for a new firm to break into, and does the old dominant firm face more or less pressure?
steps.right: Easier to enter, more pressure on the dominant firm
steps.wrong: No change, the dominant firm faces the same pressure
steps.hint: More firms trading in the market means more rivals competing for customers.

steps.right: No, their costs per unit stay higher
steps.wrong: Yes, scale makes no difference to costs
